svg.title: Outlook connector architecture
svg.desc: Three short-lived entry points: the MCP server (one stdio process per agent session), the local UI (started on demand), and the sign-in command. MCP and UI are thin surfaces over one service layer, which holds every domain decision and uses Pydantic domain models. The service calls the remote layer and local SQLite store. Graph handles mail-data reads, attachment downloads, verification and calendar windows; OWS handles mail changes, inbox rules, event details and the calendar fallback; Search v2 finds calendar events; Cloud Settings handles native signatures. Tokens come from Entra ID through the shared lrh-m365-auth cache, encrypted and locked across processes. The store keeps only the folder cache and account binding.
svg.text: Graph mail and calendar · OWS changes, rules and events · Search v2 events · Cloud Settings signatures · minimal local state
outlook-connector mcp · one stdio process per agent session
Started by Claude Code, Codex or Copilot on demand
outlook-connector ui · started by you when needed
surfaces/web/: Starlette JSON API + static JS
Mail reads and exports only · in-memory filter · download
Localhost only · exits on Ctrl+C or idle timeout
mcp, ui and auth are short-lived and
may run at the same time. They share only
service/ · every domain decision; validates input once at the entry point; never sees HTTP or wire JSON
domain/models.py: the single schema for service, MCP and web · domain/errors.py · domain/time.py: a time without a zone is UTC
remote/ · the only code that knows wire formats and ids; one adapter per port
lrh-m365-auth · profiles shared by every lrh-* Microsoft 365 connector · encrypted · locked
first-party public clients · no app registration
Surfaces never call remote/ or store/ directly.
